CONGRANT.TITLE: Texas Sea Grant College Program
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
- Preproposal submitted -

The proposed project is to develop electrically conductive concrete pipes to remove soluble cationic contaminants from run-off water via electrochemical precipitation and to protect Texas water resources including the ocean water. Concrete pipes can become conductive with added graphite and precipitate soluble cations by binding with carbonate or hydroxide at the elevated pH around the cathodic conductive concrete pipes. Metallic anodes will be used in combination. The research team will look at the removal of water hardness and heavy metals (e.g., lead, chromium-6) by the proposed novel technology. Previous research at the PI’s lab has shown that the concrete block with graphite additives as a cathode can remove 20-30% of water hardness with titanium as an anode (Billah and Kim, 2020). This study needs to be expanded to gauge the applicability to treat contaminated run-off water thus protecting Texas natural water resources including the Gulf of Mexico. The specific objectives of the project are to:

1) Determine the optimum operational conditions (voltage, ampere, graphite contents, the distance between electrodes, etc.) of the electrically conductive concrete for the most efficient hardness removal.
2) Check if the electrically conductive concrete pipes can be used to remove hardness from the tap water under both batch and continuous flow conditions. Also, focuses will be given to changes in the concentration of chlorine disinfectant and acidity of tap water.
3) Check if other soluble heavy metals in the tap water can be removed from the electrically conductive concrete pipe operated under optimum conditions that will be determined from Task 1.
4) Provide the preliminary version of construction, installation, and operational/maintenance guidance.

CONGRANT.TITLE: MRI: Acquisition of a 3D X-ray Computed Tomography for Multidisciplinary Materials Research in South Texas
Electrochemical precipitation of tap water from Lower Rio Grande Valley area with conductive concrete pipes.
CONGRANT.SPONORG: EPA Annual P3 Awards: A National Student Design Competition Focusing on People, Prosperity and the Planet
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Objective: Tap water in LRGV is extremely hard with more than 350 mg/L as CaCO3. Also, there have been reports about heavy metals in drinking water in rural communities in Lower Rio Grande Valley (LRGV) area. Thus, residents in the region depended on bottled water and watermill for drinking water, which has imposed an economical burden on them. More so is witnessed from the economically depressed area like Colonias. The proposed project is designed to remove soluble cations like water hardness and heavy metals from the tap water to ensure economical, safe, and sustainable water resources to all the local municipalities in the LRGV area. The project team proposes to develop a novel in-situ electrochemical precipitation (EP) using conductive concrete pipes as a cathode and a metallic anode. If combined with solar power, the proposed technology will be an eco-friendly water softening and cleaning system with minimum maintenance.
Description: The proposed P3 project will focus on developing a novel in-situ EP technology to remove soluble metallic contaminants from drinking water. It involves using conductive concrete as a cathode and a metallic anode in a batch or continuous flow condition. The research team in this proposal have been investigating water hardness removal using conductive concrete and metallic anode subjected to a range of power input. Previous project results from the PI’s lab showed 30% hardness removal at 15 V for 1 hr. trial. This project will expand the study to remove water hardness and soluble heavy metals like lead and chromium-6 without impairing the safety of drinking water. Also, the proposed technology will not require expensive water treatment facilities or extensive water pipe replacement. If combined with renewable solar power, it will be completely off the grid thus making the project eco-friendlier.
Results:
The project team will obtain the following information in optimizing the EP system using conductive concrete: 1) the optimum operating condition under batch and continuous flowing conditions, 2) system design parameters to treat extremely hard tap water, 3) heavy metal removal efficiency. Special care will be taken for data quantity and quality including redundant data collection and statistical analysis for data reliability.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Synthesis of Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) for Applications in Texas
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Among the groups of High-Performance Fiber-Reinforced Cementitious Composites (HPFRCC), Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) is a special type that is characterized by high-ductility (3-5% of strain) and moderate tensile strength (4-6 MPa) with 1.5-2% fiber contents by volume. Under tensile deformation, ECC shows a strain-hardening behavior and closely spaced microcracks after the first cracking. ECC has excellent shear capacity, improved damage tolerance, ability to control crack width, and synergistic interaction with reinforcing bars. The initial cost of ECC is higher than the regular concrete, but the use of ECC may reduce the life-cycle cost and corresponding environmental impact and provide improved safety because of the superior ductility.
The objective of this project is to identify the applications in which the use of ECC can be applicable in Texas transportation system. To achieve this goal, the performing agency shall conduct seven tasks categorized into three activities: (1) a comprehensive literature review with in-depth meta-analyses, (2) a survey for state, federal, and international agencies, and (3) a cost-benefit analysis considering Texas environment, life-cycle cost, and environmental impact. Based on the collected data and analysis, the recommendations on ECC applications in Texas and considerations in mixture-design, production, and constructions of ECC shall be provided.

CONGRANT.TITLE: BORDER 2020: US-Mexico Border Environmental Program RFP No. : SOLTA-C-19-013
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Project Objectives
The objective of the project is to provide technical, economic, and environmental information on various recycling methods of shredded scrap tires in quantified manner. A comprehensive literature review shall be conducted including the state-of-the-art, state-of-the-practice, and case examples of TDR aggregate. To understand the current conditions of scrap tire recycling, a survey shall be made for the engineers and local government employees in LRGV area. Based on the collected information, the project team shall compare the economic and environmental impacts of each recycling method through a systematic cost-benefit analysis and environmental evaluation.

CONGRANT.TITLE: BORDER 2020: US-Mexico Border Environmental Program RFP No. : SOLTA-C-19-013
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Scrap tire chips will be tested as an alternative to coarse aggregate media in the septic tank drain field. This will help the U.S.-Mexico border region decide if it’s feasible to use scrap tires in place of expensive aggregate for the septic tank drain fields. Also, the contaminant removal capability of scrap tire chips will be tested to address its superior applicability to the onsite wastewater treatment like a septic tank. This project will ultimately promote sustainable materials and waste management and clean sites [Goal 3].

CONGRANT.TITLE: Sustainable Waste Material Management
CONGRANT.SPONORG: EPA BORDER 2020: US-Mexico Border Environmental Program RFP No. : SOLTA-C-19-013
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Waste management is one of the most critical problems in various regions in the U.S. especially in the Lower Rio Grande Valley (LRGV) in the southernmost Texas on the border with Tamaulipas in Mexico. The U.S. produces 220 million tons of waste annually with an average of 2.1 kg per person each day (https://www.conserve-energy-future.com, 2019). The population in the LGRV is 1.2 million people with an estimated annual waste production of 2,500 tons annually. Traditional waste management refers to the activities used to manage waste from its inception until its final disposal. These activities include collection, transport, treatment and disposal of waste together with monitoring and regulation. However, most waste management strategies- if effective - remain unsustainable. Another contributor to the  problem is that the current trend in manufacturing adopts the concept of throw-away consumerism in attempt to maximize the profit by producing one-time use products (https://www.conserve-energy-future.com, 2019). With many companies on the Texan/Mexican borders, there is a need for sustainable waste management strategies that focus on the reuse, recycling, and reducing the use of environmentally friendly materials. In LRGV, with the poor economic conditions, the aging infrastructure, and with approximately 15–20% of residents living in colonias, the problem of waste management exacerbates; and the concept of sustainable waste management strategies is nearly inexistent.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Electrochemical Precipitation
Constitutive behaviors of steel fiber reinforced concrete under uniaxial compression and tension

INTELLCONT_AUTH.INSTITUTION: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Full-range constitutive curves for steel fiber reinforced concrete (SFRC) mixtures under both uniaxial compression and uniaxial tension are generally unavailable in the literature. Two types of the SFRC (straight and hooked fibers) with various fiber volume contents under uniaxial compression and tension were investigated. The results showed that the fibers remarkably enhanced the concrete post-cracking behaviors in terms of achieving higher ductility, residual strength, and toughness under compression and tension. The data collected in this study and that from the existing publications were used to evaluate the effect of steel fibers on various constitutive parameters of SFRC via statistical hypothesis tests. It was statistically evident that the tensile strength, and the strain at the peak load under either compression or tension are positively correlated with the fiber reinforcing index (RI), while there is no sufficient evidence indicating that the modulus of elasticity and compressive strength can be correlated with the RI. Finally, the constitutive behaviors of the studied mixtures were idealized, and the strain and stress coefficients from the idealized curves showed reasonably good correlations with the RI.
